html:
The Bougainville conflict was a civil war on the island of Bougainville from 1988 to 1998, between the Bougainville Revolutionary Army and the government of Papua New Guinea. Thousands died, many from a blockade that cut off medicine.

It began with landowners' anger at the huge Panguna copper mine, opened in 1972, which poured waste into rivers while profits went abroad. Led by Francis Ona, rebels shut the mine in 1989.

A truce in 1998 and a peace agreement in 2001 gave the island autonomy. In 2019 nearly all voters chose independence in a non-binding referendum, and talks with the national government go on. The war echoed the Tensions in the neighbouring Solomon Islands. See also German New Guinea and Ok Tedi.
